issue: Does the Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause apply to statements a prosecutor makes in closing argument?

sides.position: The Confrontation Clause applies to closing arguments. It is violated when a prosecutor tells the jury that an absent witness would have given inculpatory testimony.
cases: United States v. Molina-Guevara, 96 F.3d 698, 703 (3d Cir. 1996)

sides.position: The Confrontation Clause does not apply to closing arguments because closing arguments are not evidence.
cases: United States v. Solis, 299 F.3d 420, 442 (5th Cir. 2002)
United States v. Miller, 982 F.3d 412, 439 (6th Cir. 2020)

quote: Other circuits are divided over whether the Confrontation Clause applies to statements in closing arguments.
cite: United States v. Lopez, 131 F.4th 1114 (10th Cir. 2025)
